label: Kimi K3.1 Pro
output:
Our student-run Winter School on Elliptic Curves and Modular Forms, held from 5–7 November 2026, concluded on Saturday after three full days at Seminar Hall 2, Department of Mathematics, Sahyadri Institute of Science, Pune. Organising it with Ketaki Joglekar and Faizan Mirza has been exhausting, instructive and rewarding.

We received 112 applications and selected 41 MSc and early-stage PhD participants from nine states, based on a statement of interest and one reference. Beyond the numbers, we will remember the questions, difficult computations and willingness to learn from one another. For many MSc students, a small school offers what a large conference often cannot: the time and confidence to stop a lecturer and ask a basic question.

We are deeply grateful to our speakers: Dr Nilesh Dharmadhikari (Hyderabad) for his lectures on Mordell–Weil, Dr Sunanda Iyer (Chennai) for her introduction to modular forms, and Dr Tomasz Wierzbicki, who joined online from Kraków, for his sessions on computations in Sage.

One highlight came when an MSc participant from Silchar spotted an error in a worked example in Dr Iyer’s notes; she corrected it live and thanked him. That exchange captured the spirit we hoped for.

Day 2 also tested us in a different way. A power cut lasting nearly two hours left laptops dead, so we moved the afternoon problem session to the canteen with two rolling whiteboards. Unexpectedly, it became the best session of the three days. The problem sessions led by PhD students worked particularly well, and this is a format we would definitely retain.

The school was supported by ₹2.4 lakh from the institute’s student initiative grant, which covered hostel accommodation and travel for 18 outstation students. We are grateful to our faculty mentor, Prof. Anuradha Venkatesan, for her guidance; to our six PhD-student volunteers who handled the TA work; and to Mr Prakash Salunke and the office staff. Mr Salunke sorted out hostel rooms at 11 pm when the booking went wrong—one of many kindnesses participants never saw.

Thank you finally to every participant for the energy and patience you brought. Slides and problem sheets will be uploaded to the department website within two weeks. We hope to return with a second edition in late 2027, subject to funding. If this week was anything to go by, there is a real need for it.
